Will Smith delivers a deeply moving, restrained, and emotionally raw performance in the 2006 drama The Pursuit of Happyness. Playing the real-life figure Chris Gardner, Smith portrays a desperate, unhoused father battling poverty while striving to secure a competitive, unpaid stockbroker internship.

While director Gabriele Muccino originally struggled to find a child actor who could handle the intense, demanding shoot, he ultimately decided to put Will’s real-life son through the exact same rigorous audition process as the other hopefuls. The studio was initially hesitant about potential nepotism, but Muccino knew no other child could replicate that raw, genuine father-son bond.

source_details.title: The Pursuit of Happyness
source_details.synopsis: The Pursuit of Happyness is a 2006 American biographical drama film directed by Gabriele Muccino and starring Will Smith as Chris Gardner, a homeless salesman. Smith's son Jaden Smith co-stars, making his film debut as Gardner's son, Christopher Jr. The screenplay by Steven Conrad is based on the best-selling 2006 memoir of the same name written by Gardner with Quincy Troupe. It is based on Gardner's nearly one-year struggle being homeless. The intentional misspelling of the film's title comes from a mural that Gardner sees on the wall outside the daycare facility his son attended.
